semantic_adjudication.basis: Supplied dossier for obligation 0044:r1:i10: NL2 requirement quote, source transition tr_0007 (llms_emp_feedback_final_0044.puml:line:18), FCSTM transition:line:36 with empty triggers and guard R45RouteToken==7, FCSTM event:Obstacle_Detected:line:7, S3 predicate receipt with verdict false and counterexample, and inspection_equivalent_facts showing Obstacle_Detected consumed only by internal transitions.
semantic_adjudication.reason: The NL clause states the system transitions 'to the EmergencyStopping state if an obstacle is detected.' The source PlantUML (line 18) formalizes this as an event-triggered transition (tr_0007, event='Obstacle Detected'). The FCSTM transition:line:36 has triggers=[] and is guarded by R45RouteToken==7 instead. The S3 predicate verdict is false with counterexample showing expected ['Obstacle Detected'] vs observed []. The structural property (event trigger on the specific InMotion-to-EmergencyStopping transition) is violated. The strongest alternative reading is that the NL specifies only a behavioral condition (transition occurs when obstacle detected) rather than a structural requirement (the transition must carry the event as trigger). The FCSTM's two-step mechanism does achieve equivalent observable behavior: the event is consumed internally and the guarded transition fires subsequently. Two competent readings remain compatible with the supplied facts: a structural reading (supported by the source's explicit event-trigger formalization) and a behavioral reading (supported by the NL text's 'if' clause language). This is undercutting because both readings are defensible from the supplied dossier; the source's structural choice is evidence for the structural reading but does not eliminate the behavioral reading of the NL itself.
semantic_adjudication.strongest_defeater: The FCSTM implements the arrival behavior through a two-step mechanism: internal substate transitions consume Obstacle_Detected and set R45RouteToken=7, then the guarded external transition (line 36) fires. The NL text 'if an obstacle is detected' could be read as specifying only the behavioral condition under which the transition occurs, rather than mandating that the specific external transition carry the event as its trigger.
semantic_adjudication.violated_obligation: The transition from InMotion to EmergencyStopping must be triggered by the Obstacle_Detected event, per the NL clause 'or to the EmergencyStopping state if an obstacle is detected' and the source transition tr_0007 which specifies event='Obstacle Detected'.

The required edge [*] -> Accelerating within InMotion scope is absent from the complete transition inventory. This is the root cause of Accelerating, Cruising, and Approaching being unreachable from the system initial state.
issues.requirement_quote: The system begins in the Accelerating substate, moving to the Cruising substate once cruising speed is reached, as indicated by the "Reached Cruising/Cruise" signal.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The source PlantUML does not explicitly draw an initial entry arrow within InMotion, so one could argue the author left it unspecified and the compiler's synthetic UnspecifiedInitial is a valid default. However, the NL explicitly states 'The system begins in the Accelerating substate', which is a normative requirement for the initial target.
issues.title: InMotion initial entry targets UnspecifiedInitial instead of Accelerating

issues.basis: NL5 segment; source transition tr_0003 (event='Reached Cruising/Cruise'); FCSTM transition:line:19 (triggers=['Reached_Cruising_Cruise'], effects=[]); PlantUML line 12: 'Accelerating --> Cruising : Reached Cruising/Cruise'
issues.expected: The transition from Accelerating to Cruising performs the effect Cruise.

issues.reason: The source signal 'Reached Cruising/Cruise' specifies 'Cruise' as the effect component (after the slash). The FCSTM transition has no effects. The required effect is absent.
issues.requirement_quote: The system begins in the Accelerating substate, moving to the Cruising substate once cruising speed is reached, as indicated by the "Reached Cruising/Cruise" signal.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The 'Cruise' text appears within the combined event name 'Reached_Cruising_Cruise', so one could argue the effect is subsumed in the event identity. However, the source notation 'event/effect' explicitly separates them.
issues.title: Missing Cruise effect on Accelerating to Cruising transition

issues.basis: NL9 segment; source state Approaching (line 10) with only 'do/Send'; FCSTM state:Approaching:line:14 with 'during abstract Send'; reference_inspection_facts W_DEAD_NAMED_ACTION for Send in Approaching
issues.expected: The Approaching state has a continuous (do/during) action representing the activity of approaching the destination.
issues.observed: FCSTM Approaching state (line 14) has only 'during abstract Send'. No separate action for 'approach the destination' exists. The source PlantUML also only specifies 'do/Send' for Approaching.
issues.reason: The NL contract extracts 'continues to approach the destination' as a required state action. Neither the source nor the FCSTM contains a named action for this behavior on the Approaching state. The source only has 'do/Send'. This is a semantic gap between the NL behavioral description and the formal model.

issues.strongest_rebuttal: The 'approach the destination' phrase in the NL may be a behavioral description of the state's purpose rather than a formal named action. The source only specifies 'do/Send' and does not formalize a separate approach action. The continuous approaching behavior may be implicit in the state's existence and its outgoing transitions.
issues.title: Missing continuous approach-the-destination action on Approaching state

issues.basis: NL2 segment; transition group NL-GROUP-NL2-1 ALT-NL2-1; source transition tr_0006; FCSTM transition:line:35 (triggers=[], guard='R45RouteToken == 6'); FCSTM event:Arrived_Stop_Send_Arrived:line:6; inspection_equivalent_facts event_consumers shows Arrived_Stop_Send_Arrived consumed only by transitions 22,23,24,28 (internal), not by transition:line:35 (external)
issues.expected: The transition from InMotion to Stopping is triggered by the Arrived event (Arrived_Stop_Send_Arrived in FCSTM event identity).
issues.observed: FCSTM transition:line:35 (InMotion -> Stopping) has triggers=[] (empty). The transition is guarded by R45RouteToken == 6 instead of being event-triggered. The Arrived_Stop_Send_Arrived event is consumed only by internal transitions (lines 22-24, 28) within InMotion substates.
issues.reason: The transition group NL-GROUP-NL2-1 ALT-NL2-1 specifies event='Arrived' for the InMotion-to-Stopping transition. The source transition tr_0006 has event='Arrived/Stop, Send Arrived'. The FCSTM transition:line:35 has no trigger, only a guard. The required event trigger is structurally absent.
issues.requirement_quote: In the InMotion state, the system can either transition to the Stopping state when it arrives, indicated by the "Arrived/Stop, Send Arrived" signal, or to the EmergencyStopping state if an obstacle is detected.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The FCSTM implements the arrival behavior through a two-step mechanism: internal substate transitions set R45RouteToken=6, then the guarded external transition fires. This is a valid implementation pattern that achieves the same observable behavior. However, the source and NL specify a direct event-triggered transition, not a guard-mediated one.
issues.title: Missing Arrived event trigger on InMotion to Stopping transition

issues.basis: NL2 segment; transition group NL-GROUP-NL2-1 ALT-NL2-2; source transition tr_0007; FCSTM transition:line:36 (triggers=[], guard='R45RouteToken == 7'); FCSTM event:Obstacle_Detected:line:7; inspection_equivalent_facts event_consumers shows Obstacle_Detected consumed only by transitions 25,26,27,29 (internal), not by transition:line:36 (external)
issues.expected: The transition from InMotion to EmergencyStopping is triggered by the Obstacle Detected event (Obstacle_Detected in FCSTM event identity).

issues.reason: The transition group NL-GROUP-NL2-1 ALT-NL2-2 specifies event='obstacle is detected' for the InMotion-to-EmergencyStopping transition. The source transition tr_0007 has event='Obstacle Detected'. The FCSTM transition:line:36 has no trigger, only a guard. The required event trigger is structurally absent.
issues.requirement_quote: In the InMotion state, the system can either transition to the Stopping state when it arrives, indicated by the "Arrived/Stop, Send Arrived" signal, or to the EmergencyStopping state if an obstacle is detected.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: As with the Stopping transition, the FCSTM uses a two-step mechanism where internal substate transitions set R45RouteToken=7, then the guarded external transition fires. This achieves the same observable behavior through a different structural pattern.
issues.title: Missing Obstacle Detected event trigger on InMotion to EmergencyStopping transition

issues.basis: NL5 states 'The system begins in the Accelerating substate'; contract binding_hints owner=InMotion target=Accelerating; FCSTM transition inventory shows only transition:line:18 ([*]→UnspecifiedInitial) as the InMotion-scoped initial edge; verify_facts proves initial-entry:transition:line:18 and refutes reachability:state:Accelerating:line:10; inspection_facts diagnostic STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL for Accelerating.
issues.expected: Within InMotion scope, an initial pseudo-state edge from [*] to Accelerating must exist so the system enters the Accelerating substate upon entering InMotion.
issues.observed: The only initial edge within InMotion scope is transition:line:18 from [*] to UnspecifiedInitial (a compiler-synthetic state). No edge from [*] to Accelerating exists in the complete InMotion-scoped transition inventory. Verify facts confirm initial-entry:transition:line:18 is proved (targeting UnspecifiedInitial) and reachability:state:Accelerating:line:10 is refuted.
issues.reason: The contract requires InMotion's initial entry to target Accelerating. The complete FCSTM transition inventory for InMotion scope contains no [*]→Accelerating edge; the sole initial edge targets the synthetic UnspecifiedInitial. This is the root structural defect that makes the entire normal operating sequence unreachable.
issues.requirement_quote: The system begins in the Accelerating substate, moving to the Cruising substate once cruising speed is reached, as indicated by the "Reached Cruising/Cruise" signal.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The source PlantUML does not explicitly draw an initial edge within InMotion; the absence could be considered an author omission rather than a model defect. However, the NL explicitly states 'The system begins in the Accelerating substate,' establishing a normative initial-entry obligation that the model must satisfy regardless of whether the source drew the edge.
issues.title: InMotion initial entry targets synthetic UnspecifiedInitial instead of required Accelerating

issues.basis: NL5 establishes Accelerating→Cruising on Reached_Cruising_Cruise; NL6 establishes Accelerating→Approaching on Approached_Decelerate; NL7 establishes Cruising→Approaching on Approached_Decelerate. Inspection event_consumers rows for both events show empty reachable_consumer_transition_refs. Verify facts: event-consumer:Reached_Cruising_Cruise and event-consumer:Approached_Decelerate are both refuted.
issues.expected: Within InMotion, at least one consumer transition for each of the events Reached_Cruising_Cruise and Approached_Decelerate must be reachable from the top-level initial entry so the normal motion-phase sequence can execute.
issues.observed: Inspection event_consumers shows: Reached_Cruising_Cruise has consumer_transition_refs=[transition:line:19] but reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[]; Approached_Decelerate has consumer_transition_refs=[transition:line:20, transition:line:21] but reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[]. Verify facts confirm both event-consumer checks are refuted. The only reachable consumer in InMotion scope is UnspecifiedInitial for Arrived_Stop_Send_Arrived and Obstacle_Detected, which are terminal-exit events, not operating-sequence events.
issues.reason: The derived contract captures the operational-coverage property independently of the initial-entry root cause. The NL establishes that the system must respond to Reached_Cruising_Cruise (by transitioning to Cruising) and Approached_Decelerate (by transitioning to Approaching) while in the InMotion operating scope. The deterministic facts show no reachable consumer exists for either event in that scope.
issues.requirement_quote: The system begins in the Accelerating substate, moving to the Cruising substate once cruising speed is reached, as indicated by the "Reached Cruising/Cruise" signal.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The unreachability is entirely caused by the initial-entry defect (transition:line:18 targeting UnspecifiedInitial). If that single defect is repaired, all operating-event consumers become reachable. This consumer-coverage gap is therefore a causal consequence rather than an independent structural defect. However, per the method protocol, owner default entry and reachable event-consumer coverage are independent frontier properties: the coverage must still be verified even after the entry is fixed, because a different repair (e.g., adding a guard or changing the entry target to a different state) could leave coverage broken.
issues.title: Events Reached_Cruising_Cruise and Approached_Decelerate have no reachable consumer within InMotion operating scope

semantic_adjudication.reason: The NL clause states the system transitions 'to the EmergencyStopping state if an obstacle is detected.' The source PlantUML (line 18) formalizes this as an event-triggered transition (tr_0007, event='Obstacle Detected'). The FCSTM transition:line:36 has triggers=[] and is guarded by R45RouteToken==7 instead. The S3 predicate verdict is false with counterexample showing expected ['Obstacle Detected'] vs observed []. The structural property (event trigger on the specific InMotion-to-EmergencyStopping transition) is violated. The strongest alternative reading is that the NL specifies only a behavioral condition (transition occurs when obstacle detected) rather than a structural requirement (the transition must carry the event as trigger). The FCSTM's two-step mechanism does achieve equivalent observable behavior: the event is consumed internally and the guarded transition fires subsequently. Two competent readings remain compatible with the supplied facts: a structural reading (supported by the source's explicit event-trigger formalization) and a behavioral reading (supported by the NL text's 'if' clause language). This is undercutting because both readings are defensible from the supplied dossier; the source's structural choice is evidence for the structural reading but does not eliminate the behavioral reading of the NL itself.
semantic_adjudication.strongest_defeater: The FCSTM implements the arrival behavior through a two-step mechanism: internal substate transitions consume Obstacle_Detected and set R45RouteToken=7, then the guarded external transition (line 36) fires. The NL text 'if an obstacle is detected' could be read as specifying only the behavioral condition under which the transition occurs, rather than mandating that the specific external transition carry the event as its trigger.
semantic_adjudication.violated_obligation: The transition from InMotion to EmergencyStopping must be triggered by the Obstacle_Detected event, per the NL clause 'or to the EmergencyStopping state if an obstacle is detected' and the source transition tr_0007 which specifies event='Obstacle Detected'.

semantic_adjudication.reason: The NL clause states the system transitions 'to the EmergencyStopping state if an obstacle is detected.' The source PlantUML (line 18) formalizes this as an event-triggered transition (tr_0007, event='Obstacle Detected'). The FCSTM transition:line:36 has triggers=[] and is guarded by R45RouteToken==7 instead. The S3 predicate verdict is false with counterexample showing expected ['Obstacle Detected'] vs observed []. The structural property (event trigger on the specific InMotion-to-EmergencyStopping transition) is violated. The strongest alternative reading is that the NL specifies only a behavioral condition (transition occurs when obstacle detected) rather than a structural requirement (the transition must carry the event as trigger). The FCSTM's two-step mechanism does achieve equivalent observable behavior: the event is consumed internally and the guarded transition fires subsequently. Two competent readings remain compatible with the supplied facts: a structural reading (supported by the source's explicit event-trigger formalization) and a behavioral reading (supported by the NL text's 'if' clause language). This is undercutting because both readings are defensible from the supplied dossier; the source's structural choice is evidence for the structural reading but does not eliminate the behavioral reading of the NL itself.
